item.material_system: rare earth luminescent materials, including lanthanide ion-doped phosphors, persistent luminescent materials, lanthanide ion-doped upconversion materials, rare earth luminescent complexes, and rare earth-relevant perovskite materials
key_findings: Rare earth luminescent materials have unique electronic configurations and numerous energy levels, which endow them with many fascinating optical properties
Applications of rare earth luminescent materials have consistently been expanded since the 1960s
High sensitivity, convenient use, rapid responses, and remote and noncontact properties are features of optical thermometers based on temperature-dependent spectroscopic properties
Rare earth luminescent materials have exhibited potential for applications in biomedicine, especially in the diagnosis and treatment of diseases

Combining UCNPs with other functional materials to construct nanocomposites and achieve synergistic effects is an important strategy for strengthening and extending the applications of rare earth luminescent materials
Rare earth luminescent materials have a wide range of application prospects, including lighting, displays, sensing, optical information storage, biomedicine, and so on
Shortwave infrared (SWIR) emission was realized by doping Cr3+-Yb3+ ion pairs into Lu0.2Sc0.8BO3 host materials
Ultrabroadband emission from lead-free halide double perovskites (DPs) was achieved by combining self-trapped exciton (STE) recombination with Ln3+ dopant-induced extra light-emitting channels
quotes: ranging from the ultraviolet (UV) to the near infrared (NIR)
have a wide range of application prospects
rare earth luminescent materials and their applications in lighting, display, information storage, sensing, and bioimaging as well as therapy
